LESSON: MOVEMENT OF MATERIALS IN AND OUT OF THE CELL

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.2: Movement of materials in and out of the cell
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Movement of materials in and out of the cell, part of Living Things and their Environment in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do materials move in and out of a cell? 2. Why do materials move in and out of the cell?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Movement of materials in and out of the cell together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner develops writing skills as the learner writes clearly and correctly while

recording findings from experiments to demonstrate osmosis using plant tissues and visking tubing.

● Creativity and imagination: Experimenting skills are developed as the learner sets-up and runs experiments to demonstrate

osmosis using plant tissues.

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates the opinions of peers when discussing the roles of diffusion and osmosis in living

things.

● Responsibility: The learner plays assigned roles while carrying out experiments to demonstrate semi-permeability

25

of the cell membrane.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Environmental Education and Climate Change: The learner handles wastes of plant materials from experiments to

demonstrate osmosis.

Link to other subjects:

● The learner is able to improve signing skills, a KSL concept, as they practice fingerspelling and signing words related to the

movement of materials in and out of the cell.

● The information on diffusion and osmosis is linked to the absorption of water and mineral salts from the soil by crops in

Agriculture and Nutrition.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Digital Devices

● Print media (charts, pictures, journals, magazines)

● Science specific signs dictionary

● Laboratory Apparatus and Equipment

● Coursebooks

● Visking tubing
